headline: Budget adjustments for FY 2026 and FY 2027, FY 28 draft budget priorities, and a foodservice bid.
summary: Items include out-of-state travel for three staff members, a New York theater field trip in April 2027, and changes to library materials policies. Members also filed orders on AI tools, a one-page overview of committee roles, and the foodservice bid.
items: Letter to lift exit assurances, received as a memo
MASC policy updates on library materials and resources, referred to Policy and Governance Subcommittee
PFA budget revision request for McMahon additional appropriation, received as a memo
Out-of-state field trip to Broadway theaters in New York on April 14, 2027
Out-of-state travel for Tim LaGrant to Whalley's Annual Technology Conference in Connecticut, November 5-6, 2026
Out-of-state travel for Laura Espinoza-Mufson and Jose Lopez to the CABE Conference in Long Beach, CA, March 10-13, 2027
Grant acceptance and warrant report for 11.9.26
Order for a list of AI tools used in the district, referred to Ad Hoc AI Subcommittee
Order for a family-friendly one-page overview of School Committee roles, referred to Parent/Caregiver and Community Engagement Ad Hoc Subcommittee
Order to discuss the upcoming foodservice bid, referred to Finance and Operations Subcommittee
Glasheen self assessment and goals, including a student learning goal for the superintendent
Cell phone connectivity in school facilities, referred to a joint City Council and School Committee subcommittee and to Finance and Operations Subcommittee
Final reading and adoption of policies BEDB, IB, ID, and FF

Or by phone by calling (301) 715-8592 and then providing Meeting ID Web 852 8777 7627. No
passcode is required.
(Spanish Interpretation will be available).
Today, March 29, 2025 Governor Maura Healey signed into law bodies to H.62, as amended
by S.2506 (which contains the final form of the bill), entitled "An act Relative to Extending
Certain Covid-19 Measures Adopted during the State of Emergency" ("ACT). Of interest to all
governmental public bodies in Massachusetts, the Act extends until June, 2027, the authority
for meetings of multiple-member bodies to be held in an entirely remote or hybrid format. All
public bodies may hold fully remote or hybrid meetings, without the physical presence of a
quorum of the public body, as long as "adequate, alternative means" of public access is also
provided.
NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN IN ACCORDANCE WITH CHAPTER 28 OF THE ACTS OF 2009,

MASSACHUSETTS GENERAL LAWS, THAT A REGULAR MEETING OF THE HOLYOKE
SCHOOL COMMITTEE WILL BE HELD ON NOVEMBER 9, 2026.

Order filed by School Committee Member Mr. Michaelsen, That the Superintendent submit a

Order filed by School Committee Member Ms. Lubold, Request that the School Committee
authorize the Parent, Caregiver, and Community Engagement Ad Hoc Subcommittee to
develop a family-friendly, accessible one-page overview explaining the roles and
responsibilities of the School Committee and its subcommittees. Existing policy language is
accurate and approved, however it is not easily accessible or engaging for general public use.
A revised one-pager would provide clearer, more approachable information suitable for
presentations, handouts, and other public-facing communication committee members can use
as appropriate .

Nov 23rd- School Committee Meeting
The listing of matters are those reasonably anticipated by the Chair which may be discussed at
the meeting. Not all items listed may in fact be discussed and other items not listed may also
be brought up for discussion to the extent permitted by law.* The Holyoke Public Schools
makes available a public discussion period for persons in the audience to address the
Committee on specific agenda items. In order to hear as many speakers as possible, the
Committee asks individuals to continue their remarks for two (2) minutes. Any person wishing
to submit longer testimony should give copies to the Committee Secretary before the meeting
so that they may be distributed to Committee members. The speaker can then summarize this
testimony at the meeting within the two (2) minute time period. Persons wishing to speak
should register with the Committee Secretary immediately before the meeting begins.
Individuals who request specific items to be included on the Committee's agenda should mail a
written request fifteen (15) days in advance of a Committee meeting date to Irene Feliciano, 57
Suffolk Street, Holyoke, MA 01040
